Theme

Latin word

ratiō

ratiō, ratiōnis f.

noun, third declension

way, method, plan; method, way; a policy, a line of conduct; method, the way something is done; a reason given, grounds; reason, the reasoning mind; method of preparation; a reckoning, a calculation; a system, a method; an order worked out by reason; a method, a way of doing something; a theory, an explanation, a system of ideas; theory, the principles (as against practice)

Examples

  • Dēceptus sum, at nōn dēfatīgātus. … Hāc nōn successit, aliā aggrediēmur viā.

    I’ve been foiled, but I’m not worn out. … That way didn’t work; we’ll try another approach.Ter. And. 669–670

    In the entry for approach

  • sed vīvimus, et aliqua vīvendī ratiō quaerenda est

    but we are alive, and some way of living must be foundQuint. 6 pr. 14

    In the entry for approach

  • haec ego ad tē ob eam causam maximē scrībō, ut jam dē tuā quoque ratiōne meditēre

    my main reason for writing this is that you should now think about your own policy tooCic. Fam. 1.8.3

    In the entry for policy

  • Dē suā ratiōne interrogātus, ambiguus fit.

  • Nec vērō habēre virtūtem satis est quasi artem aliquam, nisi ūtāre; etsī ars quidem, cum eā nōn ūtāre, scientiā tamen ipsā tenērī potest, virtūs in ūsū suī tōta posita est

    Nor is it enough to have virtue as one has some art, unless you use it; for an art, even when you do not use it, can still be held by knowledge alone, but virtue lies wholly in its useCic. Rep. 1.2
